notes: Explicit source-scoped office P39 → jurisdiction classification only. Neither GIS, geographic borders, sovereignty for all years, political influence, ethnicity nor legal succession is inferred. New contexts are independent overlays, never SQL canonical states.

contexts.label: Electoral college of Holy Roman Empire
contexts.caveat: Electoral dignity is neither a sovereign territory nor the imperial office itself.

contexts.label: Kingdom of Bohemia crown
contexts.caveat: Bohemian crown is separately held; composite Habsburg association is not state identity.

contexts.label: Kingdom of Hungary crown
contexts.caveat: Hungarian crown not identical to Habsburg composite or Austrian modern citizenship.

contexts.label: Andorran co-principality
contexts.caveat: French co-prince is joint Andorran office, not a claim that Andorra is part of France.

contexts.label: Politburo of CPSU Central Committee
contexts.caveat: Politburo membership is institutional and does not establish personal sovereign authority.

contexts.label: Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union (all-Union legislature)
contexts.caveat: Deputy membership of the USSR legislature is not the chair of its Presidium, a republican Supreme Soviet, a head-of-state office or a claim of actual political dominance.

contexts.label: Swedish monarchy
contexts.caveat: World-pilot Swedish polity is a reference context, not a modern boundary.

contexts.label: Spanish monarchy
contexts.caveat: World-pilot Spain context; office type not guaranteed unchanged in every period.

contexts.label: King of France and Navarre office scope
contexts.caveat: A compound royal style; do not automatically infer a geographic union or collapse Navarre into France.

contexts.label: First French Empire after 1804
contexts.caveat: Empire after 1804 is not the French Republic in the 1762–1800 pilot, even if ruled by same person.

contexts.label: Council of People's Commissars of USSR (Union government)
contexts.caveat: Union Sovnarkom until 15 March 1946: not the RSFSR Sovnarkom, a modern state or a personal ruler. Government chair and deputy are different offices. Title window is not an independently proved personal appointment.

contexts.label: Council of Ministers of USSR (Union government)
contexts.caveat: Post-1946 Union Council of Ministers: separate successor title but institutional continuity under the law. Ordinary deputy and FIRST deputy are separate rank types, neither is Chairman. The 15 March naming law is not a blanket 15 March appointment for each person.

offices.caveat: Elector dignity has a vote, not necessarily one-person sovereignty over Holy Roman Empire.
Separate Bohemian royal title; not an interchangeable Habsburg/Austrian office.
Separate Hungarian royal title; no inference of ethnic origin or all-territory control.
Andorran joint head office; never make Andorra French territory by P39 alone.
Party committee membership, neither president nor sole effective head.

Candidate Politburo member is a nonvoting party-body status, NOT full Politburo membership Q108495011, head of state or proof of factual sole control. Historical title changes and year boundaries require source review.
Deputy/member of the all-Union Supreme Soviet, a legislative representative; not chairman of the body, chairman of its Presidium, or independent state ruler. No terms inferred from this office type.
Legal monarch of Sweden; distinct from dukedom held before accession.
Spanish royal title; distinguish 18th-century kingdom from modern state context.
French and Navarre compound office title; source-specific juridical context.
Napoleonic emperor office begins after 1800; not first-consul office in the 1799–1800 pilot.
Ordinary deputy chairman of Union Council of People's Commissars before 1946; NOT chairman of USSR/RSFSR governments, NOT successor Council of Ministers deputy, NOT first deputy.
Ordinary deputy chairman of USSR Council of Ministers after the 1946 law; not Chairman or First Deputy. Source dates and continuity require independent verification.

FIRST deputy Chairman of Union Council of Ministers after 1946, higher formal rank than ordinary deputy Q134373912 but not head of government Q4376674. May be held by several people; does not prove real political dominance.
